items.title: Push Square's spoiler-free tips: accessibility toggles, classic controls and $100 fast travel
items.summary: Push Square's 12-tip guide covers turning on Accessible Combat and Reduced Vehicle Damage in Settings, switching back to the Classic GTA 5 control scheme, skipping a RydeMe ride for $100 to fast travel, banking wallet cash at BuckMe ATMs so it is not lost when busted or wasted, and registering a stolen car at Pay 'N' Spray to keep it for good.

items.title: Rockstar leaves sex workers out of GTA VI for the first time in 25 years
items.summary: Consequence reports Rockstar told Shacknews the feature was left out to keep the focus on Jason and Lucia's couple-on-the-run story, carrying forward systems like the wanted system, radio, robberies and car theft instead; strip clubs are still in the game.

items.title: Rockstar co-founder Sam Houser issues a rare statement for launch
items.summary: GameSpot reports Houser marked launch with a rare statement given to GamesRadar+, saying Rockstar tried to make a game that exceeds expectations and shows what the medium can do, hoping GTA VI feels familiar and entirely new and is fun above all, and looking forward to many more years of sharing these experiences.

items.title: Rockstar posts set times for GTA VI: The Festival in Miami on November 21
items.summary: TalkEsport covers Rockstar's November 18 post with the full two-stage running order for Mana Wynwood: doors 4 p.m. through 2 a.m., Cardi B at 7:45 p.m., Metro Boomin at midnight and a Cactus Jack set headlined by Travis Scott closing from 12:40 to 2 a.m., with all ticket proceeds going to local Miami charities.

items.title: VGC's beginner's guide: six tips for your first hours in Leonida
items.summary: VGC's starter guide covers stashing cash under the floorboards in Jason's bedroom until the Buck Me mission opens a bank account, using the minimap to spot hidden rooms and enterable buildings, feeding Jason's snake for an early Focus buff, and calling a mechanic for roadside repairs once that unlocks.

items.title: GameSpot picks five things to do first in GTA 6
items.summary: GameSpot recommends buying a suppressor at the Key Lento Ammu-Nation, exploring Key Lento and clearing its side content before moving on, saving toward a garage once garages unlock, and not stressing about early money since the story drains both accounts in the first stretch.

items.title: Reviews are in: GTA VI lands a 99 on Metacritic, tying the all-time record
items.summary: The review embargo lifted at 6 a.m. ET on November 18 and the first verdicts are near-unanimous: a 99 Metascore from 100 critic reviews on PS5, tying Ocarina of Time for the highest ever, and 98 on OpenCritic with every critic recommending it. IGN, GamesRadar+, VGC and The Guardian are among the perfect scores, with the locked 30fps target the most common complaint.

items.title: GTA VI is officially out in New Zealand — spoiler warning for everyone still waiting
items.summary: Polygon reports the rolling midnight launch has begun: New Zealand players got in from 6 a.m. ET on November 18 while the US waits for midnight local time on November 19, so early-game spoilers will be circulating on social media and streams all day Wednesday.

items.title: Miami Heat host a Vice City night on launch eve, drone show included
items.summary: USA Today reports the Heat will turn tonight's game against Milwaukee into 'A Night in Vice City' — neon Cactus Jack jerseys, a themed court, soundtrack music and the game's fast-food brands at concessions in the Kaseya Center, capped by a drone show over Biscayne Bay; doors open at 5 p.m. ET ahead of a 7 p.m. tipoff.

items.title: Rockstar promotes GTA VI in China, where it still has no sales approval
items.summary: Reuters reports Rockstar is promoting GTA VI to about 480,000 followers on its verified Douyin account ahead of Thursday's launch, even though the game has no official approval for sale in mainland China and is absent from the approved-import lists, leaving fans to overseas editions and imported copies.

items.title: Launch day arrives after a 13-year wait, with a new cast name confirmed
items.summary: The Associated Press marks GTA VI becoming playable at midnight local time on Thursday, starting in New Zealand, where provider Chorus expects about 35 petabytes of extra traffic from the 212 GB download; actor Stephen Root also confirmed to AP that he appears in the game, though Rockstar has not identified his role.

items.title: GTA Online players plan a 'last ride' through Los Santos on launch eve
items.summary: Le Monde reports GTA Online regulars will gather on the evening of November 18 for a final group drive through Los Santos hours before GTA VI launches, with the Grand Theft Hamlet creators reuniting their troupe; GTA VI launches single-player only, so the old Online — estimated at over 20 million monthly players in 2024 — is not shutting down.

items.title: Rockstar tribunal reaches closing submissions in Glasgow, two days before launch
items.summary: Claimants' lawyers told a Glasgow employment tribunal on November 17 that Rockstar's 2025 dismissals of 34 workers were 'shock and awe' tactics over union organizing, while Rockstar's written submissions call them fair dismissals for misconduct; Rockstar's closing is due November 18, no ruling date has been set, and a separate UK union recognition vote runs to November 26.

items.title: Justice say GTA VI will probably be their first and last video game score
items.summary: In an interview translated by Eurogamer, GTA VI composers Justice — Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay — say they took the job thinking it would likely be the only game score they ever do, and that the music had to stand up on its own outside the game as well as in it.

items.title: GTA VI leads The Game Awards with eight nominations, including Game of the Year
items.summary: The Game Awards announced its 2026 nominees on November 17, and GTA VI leads with eight nods — Game of the Year, Best Game Direction, Narrative, Art Direction, Score and Music, Audio Design and Action/Adventure, plus Best Performance for Manni L. Perez — ahead of the December 10 show.
